title: Forget on purpose: agent memory, autonomous exploits, open-model limits
summary: Google catches the first exploit pipeline running with no human in the loop, OpenAI lets four outside assessors in under negotiated terms, Qwen4-Max arrives cheap but closed, and a new paper explains why AI job losses show up in the statistics years before job creation. The deep dive covers Anthropic's agent-memory experiments: why strong models write less, why rigid memory rules backfire, and how offline "dreaming" catches notes that have gone wrong.
shownotes:
Google GTIG finds exploit_agent, a fully autonomous patch-diff-to-exploit pipeline, in the wild
OpenAI's first phase of embedded assessments with Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire
Qwen4-Max: $1.50/$4.50 per million tokens, 1M context, closed weights
Esposito & Zhang: AI and the two margins of work, why job losses show up before job creation
Deep dive: Anthropic's components of agent memory, note-taking as prediction, rigid rules, dreaming, wiki vs search, failure modes
